column14: From Kitale take the signposted murram Endebess road to Chorlim Gate, the park's main gate and headquarters (about 15 km from Kitale per secondary sources). The campsite is reached on internal park tracks; get directions from the gate.
column16: Tracks are slippery and muddy in the rains.
column21: Special campsite: reserve well in advance for exclusive use through the park warden or KWS reservations (reservations@kws.go.ke).
column24: No facilities: bring water, a source of fire and kitchen equipment (KWS). Most special campsites are near rivers; a Tripadvisor reviewer describes the park's special campsite as having a brook running through it.
column25: Listed as the park's only special campsite on KWS Mt Elgon page and 2026 brochure.

column14: From Kitale drive 22 km north on the A1 towards Kapenguria to Kipsaina junction, then 5 km on a signposted murram road to Saiwa Gate, the only entrance; the campsite is near the gate and Tree Top Hut.
column16: Final murram stretch can be muddy after rain.
column21: KWS public campsite: no advance booking normally needed; pay at Saiwa Gate or via KWS eCitizen/KWSPay (reservations@kws.go.ke for enquiries).
column23: water; toilets; bathroom; communal kitchen; electricity; two thatched shelters; benches; barbecue grill
column24: Large open grassy site overlooking the swamp (2022 trip report). The park is walking-only along trails and boardwalks. Benches and barbecue grill from the map note; electricity and shelters per Wikivoyage.
column25: Listed on KWS Saiwa page (2026); Wikivoyage entry updated Aug 2026; visited by overlanders in 2022.

column14: From Kakamega town take the Kakamega–Webuye highway about 15–18 km north-east to the signposted turn-off; Buyangu Gate and the KWS office are about 600 m off the main road, with Udo's bandas and campsite just inside.
column15: tarmac to the turn-off, then short murram access
column16: High rainfall; access track and campsite can be muddy in the March–May and October–November rains.
column21: KWS public campsite: pay on arrival at Buyangu Gate (KWS eCitizen/KWSPay); enquiries via KWS (customerservice@kws.go.ke).
column23: water; communal kitchen/cooking shelter; ablution block; designated fire area
column24: Sits beside Udo's Bandas in the Buyangu (northern) section of the reserve. Open fires only in the designated zone. Motor vehicles are restricted to the track to Buyangu Hill; forest trails are on foot, and guides are available at the gate. Facilities per KWS map note and Wikivoyage; current condition not confirmed by a recent trip report.
column25: Listed as a public campsite on KWS Kakamega Forest page (2026); OSM node 'Udo's Campsite'.
column30: A calm rainforest campsite in Kakamega with working if ageing facilities and rich bird and monkey life.
column31: Hot showers, taps and power at shelters; Colobus monkeys and abundant birdlife; Quiet forest setting with guided walks nearby
column32: Infrastructure is old and run down; Damp; one reviewer found mould in the guesthouse; Hard to find a flat pitch
